outcome: Present relevant, eligible products and service actions across channels while respecting consent, preference, suitability, frequency, and customer control.
overview: Batch campaigns and disconnected journeys flood Gulf shoppers with irrelevant offers, driving opt-outs, rising acquisition costs and wasted media spend. This solution assembles a real-time customer context across web, app, store and loyalty channels, applies consent and eligibility rules before any model runs, then ranks the next best product or service action for each interaction — in Arabic or English. Unsuitable or out-of-stock offers are suppressed, contact frequency is capped, and every recommendation carries a reason. A 6–10 week controlled pilot on one channel measures incremental conversion against a holdout, proving value without dark patterns, discrimination or privacy compromise.

benefits.text: Improve incremental conversion or contribution on the pilot channel in a controlled test
benefits.source: Redington Retail catalogue; consistent with published personalisation benchmark ranges
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Uplift to validate against a holdout on the customer’s own traffic during the pilot — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Reduce irrelevant contacts, opt-outs and wasted campaign spend
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Depends on consent coverage, identity resolution and catalogue data quality

benefits.text: Honour 100% of consent, eligibility and frequency rules by design, with an auditable reason per action
benefits.source: Reference design — policy-first gating before ranking
benefits.limits: A design property verified in consent tests; it depends on the customer’s consent records being accurate

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); customer and consent data remain in the customer tenancy in the reference designs

notFor.situation: No consent management or reliable consent records for marketing use
notFor.why: The design gates every action on consent; without trustworthy records nothing can honestly be recommended

notFor.situation: No customer identity resolution across the channels in scope
notFor.why: Next-best-action needs one view of the customer; fragmented identities produce contradictory offers

notFor.situation: No capacity to run controlled experiments with a holdout
notFor.why: Incrementality is the only honest measure of personalisation value; before/after correlation is not accepted

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns marketing policy, consent records and experiment approval · Duration: 6–10 weeks pilot; further 14–24 weeks to omnichannel scale
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, decisioning specialist, data scientist; customer marketing owner, e-commerce lead, privacy officer, analytics lead · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Discovery and baseline agreement
2) Consent and eligibility rule configuration
3) Channel and catalogue integration
4) Experiment design and pilot launch
5) Weekly outcome and harm review
6) Benefit review and handover
